key_insight: EHRFlow learns continuous patient trajectories from irregular EHR data by conditioning flow-matching dynamics on prior patient history, enabling more realistic future forecasting.
clinical_relevance: This could improve long-range prediction of clinical codes and support patient trajectory modeling at arbitrary time horizons, including intervention-aware simulations.
method: Encodes a patient's prior clinical history as model context.
Uses multi-marginal flow matching to model continuous-time latent dynamics from irregular observations.
Forecasts future clinical events while allowing conditional guidance for counterfactual scenarios.
evidence_signal: The authors report improved horizon-averaged top-5 clinical-code accuracy on synthetic benchmarks and on real-world datasets with more than one million patients, including external validation.
watch_item: Performance gains in retrospective and simulated settings may not fully translate to prospective clinical use, especially if data quality, coding practices, or treatment patterns differ.
paper_title: Learning Continuous Patient Trajectories from Electronic Health Records
